δύ εται ὁ ἥλιο ἐπὶ τοὺ προφήτα ὑμῶν με ημβρία , οὕτως καὶ δύει ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς
ἁμαρτάνοντας, οὐ χαριζόμενος αὐτοῖς ἔτι ἁμαρτάνουσι τὴν ἰδίαν ἀνατολήν.
ἐντέλλεται οὖν ἡμῖν ὁ Παῦλος μὴ ποιῆσαι τοιαῦτα κατὰ τὴν ὀργὴν ὡς ἐπιδῦναι ἡμῖν
τὸν ἥλιον καὶ γενέσθαι ἐν ταῖς ψυχαῖς ἡμῶν νύκτα. 20 Eph. iv27 [μηδὲ δίδοτε τόπον
τῷ διαβόλῳ.] [Ὠριγένης δέ φησιν] ὅμοιον τοῦτό ἐστι τῷ ἐν τῷ Ἐκκλησιαστῇ
εἰρημένῳ, ἐὰν πνεῦμα τοῦ ἐξου ιά ζοντο ἀναβῇ ἐπί ε τόπον ου μὴ ἀφῇ , ὅτι ἴαμα
καταπαύ ει ἁμαρτία μεγάλα . τόπον δὲ δίδομεν τῷ διαβόλῳ ἢ τῷ ἐξου ιάζοντι
πνεύματι ἀναβάντι ἐφ' ἡμᾶς, ὅτε οὐ πεπλήρωται ἡμῶν τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν ἁγίων
μαθημάτων ἢ τῆς σωτηρίου πίστεως καὶ λογισμῶν διαφερόντων καὶ
συμβουλευόντων ἡμῖν τὰ ἄριστα· κατὰ γὰρ τὸν πατέρα Ἰωάννου Ζαχαρίαν ἐπὶ τὰ
κλίματα τῆ ψυχῆ ἐπι κηνοῖ ὁ Σατανᾶ , καὶ αἱ τοιαίδε συγκαταθέσεις τοῖς χείροσι καὶ
ῥοπαὶ ἐπὶ τὰς συγκαταθέσεις προκαλοῦνται τὸν διάβολον εἰσελθεῖν ἡμῶν εἰς τὰς
ψυχάς. καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ Ἰούδα γοῦν γέγραπται τοῦ προδότου, πρότερον μὲν τοῦ διαβόλου
ἤδη βεβληκότο εἰ τὴν καρδίαν ἵνα παραδῷ αὐτὸν Ἰούδα Σίμωνο Ἰ καριώτη , μετὰ
δὲ ταῦτα ὅτι μετὰ τὸ ψωμίον εἰ ῆλθεν εἰ ἐκεῖνον ὁ Σατανᾶ · ὡς εἰ, βεβληκότο τοῦ
διαβόλου εἰ τὴν καρδίαν Ἰούδα ἵνα παραδῷ τὸν Κύριον, πρὸς τὸ βληθὲν στὰς ὁ
Ἰούδας ἦν, οὐκ ἂν ὕστερον εὑρήκει τόπον εἰς αὐτὸν εἰ ελθεῖν ὁ Σατανᾶ . [ iv 28] ὁ
κλέπτων μηκέτι κλεπτέτω, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ κοπιάτω ἐργαζόμενος τὸ ἀγαθὸν ταῖς
χερσίν, ἵνα ἔχῃ μεταδιδόναι τῷ χρείαν ἔχοντι. ἐπείπερ ἐν ταῖς τοῦ βίου πραγματείαις
ἀναστρεφόμενοι προφάσει τοῦ πορισμοῦ τῶν ἐπιτηδείων καὶ πολλοὶ τῶν
πεπιστευκέναι νομιζομένων, κἂν δοκῶσι καθαρεύειν ἀπὸ εἰδωλολατρείας καὶ πάσης
πορνείας, οὐκ εὐκόλως ἀφίστανται τοῦ κλέπτειν ἐν τῷ ὠνεῖσθαι καὶ πιπράσκειν καὶ
συμπραγμα τεύεσθαί τισι, διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ὤκνησεν, ὡς ἔτι κλεπτόντων (καὶ ταῦτα ἐν
Ἐφέσῳ) τινῶν, οἱονεὶ ἐλέγξαι ὡς εἰδὼς τοὺς τοιούτους· τὸν δὲ δίκαιον πορισμὸν
δηλοῖ αὐτὸ τὸ ἐργαζόμενος τὸ ἀγαθόν, τῶν μὲν ἀδίκως ποριζόντων οὐ τὸ ἀγαθὸν
ἀλλὰ τὸ πονηρὸν ἐργαζομένων, τῶν δὲ μετ' εὐλαβείας περιποιούντων αὐτοῖς τὰ
ἀναγκαῖα καὶ ἐν τούτῳ τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἐργαζομένων. 21 Eph. iv29 [πᾶς λόγος σαπρὸς ἐκ
τοῦ στόματος ὑμῶν μὴ ἐκπορευέσθω ἀλλ' εἴ τις ἀγαθὸς πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῆς χρείας
ἵνα δῷ χάριν τοῖς ἀκούουσιν.] [Ὠριγένης φησίν] ἀγαθὸς λόγος ἐστὶ πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν
τῆς χρείας διδοὺς χάριν τοῖς ἀκούουσιν ὁ διδασκαλικὸς καὶ ἐπ' ἀρετὴν μὲν
προτρεπτικὸς κακίας δὲ ἀποστερητικός· σαπρὸς δέ, ὁ συναύξων τὴν κακίαν καὶ
ἐρεθίζων ἐπὶ τὰ χείρονα. [ iv 30] καὶ μὴ λυπεῖτε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἐν ᾧ
ἐσφραγίσθητε εἰς ἡμέραν ἀπολυτρώσεως. εἴπερ ἡ λύπη πάθος ἐστί, καὶ καλῶς
ἀποδίδοται περὶ αὐτῆς ὅτι ἐστὶ «δόξα πρόσφατος κακοῦ παρουσίας ἐφ' ᾧ καθήκει
συστέλλεσθαι,» οὔτε δὲ δοξάζει τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα οὔτε (ἵνα δοθῇ δοξάζειν) δοξάζει τὸ
κακὸν αὐτῷ παρεῖναι, οὐ λυπήσεται τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα. μήποτ' οὖν, τὸ ὅσον ἐφ' ἡμῖν,
τάδε πράττοντες λυποῦμεν τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα τοῦ Θεοῦ; καὶ ὁ Κύριος δέ φησιν ἐν τῷ
Ἰεζεκιήλ καὶ ἐν πᾶ ι τούτοι ἐλύπε ἐμέ. τὰ δὲ πολλάκις ἡμῖν εἰρημένα περὶ ὀργῆς καὶ
θυμοῦ ὕπνου τε καὶ τῶν ἀνθρωποπαθῶν φωνῶν χρήσιμα καὶ εἰς τὸν λόγον τὸν περὶ
τοῦ μὴ λυπεῖτε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τοῦ Θεοῦ. ἐσφραγίσθημεν δὲ τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι,
ἵνα τὸν τύπον τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος δεξάμενοι, ἀμερίστου μείναντος τοῦ
σφραγίσαντος, τοὺς τύπους λαβόντες τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἅγιοι γενώμεθα, καὶ τὸ
πνεῦμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καθ' ἕκαστον ἡμῶν τὸ ἐν ἡμῖν ἅγιον γένηται, οἶμαι δὲ ὅτι καὶ
ἡ ψυχή. τῷ πνεύματι μὲν οὖν τῷ ἁγίῳ ὁ σφραγιζόμενος σφραγίζεται, ὁ δὲ Θεός ἐστιν
ὁ σφραγίζων. σφραγίζεται δὲ ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι πᾶς ὁ ἐκ τοῦ
πιστεύειν τῷ Θεῷ φραγί α ὅτι ἀληθή ἐ τιν ὁ Θεό · καὶ σφραγίζεται ἵνα τηρήσας τὴν
σφραγῖδα καὶ δείξας αὐτὴν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ἀπολυτρώσεως ἄθραυστον τοῖς
ἀπολυτρουμένοις συναριθμηθῇ. 22 Eph. iv31 πᾶσα πικρία καὶ θυμὸς καὶ ὀργὴ καὶ
κραυγὴ καὶ βλασφημία ἀρθήτω ἀφ' ὑμῶν σὺν πάσῃ κακίᾳ. [Ὠριγένης φησίν] γενικὸν
μέν τινες πάθος ᾠήθησαν εἶναι τὴν ὀργήν, καὶ αὐτὴν τάξαντες ὑπὸ γένος τὴν
ἐπιθυμίαν· καὶ ὅρον γε ἀποδεδώκασι τῆς ὀργῆς τοιοῦτον «ὀργή ἐστιν ἐπιθυμία
τιμωρίας τοῦ δοκοῦντος οὐ προσηκόντως ἠδικηκέναι.» εἴδη δὲ πολλὰ τῆς ὀργῆς
ἀναγράψαντες, συγκατατάττουσιν αὐτοῖς τὴν πικρίαν μὲν εἶναι ὀργὴν
δυσπαράδεκτον ἢ παραχρῆμα ἐκρηγνυμένην (εἰλῆφθαι δέ φασι τὸ δυσπαράδεκτον
pass_a_gloss: the sun will set upon your prophets at midday, so it also sets upon all those sinning, not granting to them while they still sin its own rising. Paul therefore orders us not to do such things according to anger as for the sun to set upon us and night to come to be in our souls. [4:27] Neither give place to the devil. Origen says: this is like what was said in Ecclesiastes: if the spirit of the one having authority goes up upon you, do not let go your place, because healing makes great sins cease. We give place to the devil or to the spirit having authority that has gone up upon us when our governing part has not been filled with holy teachings or with the saving faith and with thoughts that distinguish and counsel us the best things; for according to Zechariah the father of John, Satan encamps upon the regions of the soul, and such assents to the worse things and inclinations toward the assents call the devil to enter into our souls. Indeed also about Judas the traitor it is written, first that the devil having already cast into the heart that Judas of Simon Iscariot should betray him, and after these things that after the morsel Satan went into that one; as if, the devil having cast into the heart of Judas that he betray the Lord, Judas had stood against what was cast, Satan would not later have found place to enter into him. [4:28] The one stealing let him steal no longer, but rather let him toil, working the good with the hands, so that he may have to share with the one having need. Since, living in the business affairs of life on the pretext of procuring the necessities, even many of those thought to have believed, even if they seem to be clean from idolatry and all fornication, do not easily stand away from stealing in buying and selling and doing business together with some, because of this he did not shrink, as though some were still stealing (and this in Ephesus), as it were to refute them as knowing such people; and the just procuring is shown by the very working the good, those who procure unjustly working not the good but the evil, and those who with reverence secure for themselves the necessities working the good also in this. [4:29] Let every rotten word not go out of your mouth, but if any is good for building up of the need, so that it may give grace to the hearers. Origen says: a good word for building up of the need giving grace to the hearers is the teaching one, and exhorting to virtue but depriving of vice; and the rotten one is the one increasing vice together with it and provoking toward the worse things. [4:30] And do not grieve the holy spirit of God, in which you were sealed for a day of redemption. If grief is a passion, and it is well rendered about it that it is a fresh opinion of presence of evil at which it is fitting to contract, and the holy spirit neither opines nor (if it be granted to opine) opines evil to be present to it, the holy spirit will not be grieved. Perhaps then, as far as in us, doing these things we grieve the holy spirit of God? And the Lord also says in Ezekiel: and in all these you grieved me. And the things often said by us about anger and wrath and sleep and the human-passion words are useful also for the account about do not grieve the holy spirit of God. And we were sealed with the holy spirit, so that having received the stamp of the holy spirit, the sealer remaining undivided, having taken the stamps of the holy spirit we may become holy, and the spirit of the man in each of us, the one in us, may become holy, and I think also the soul. With the holy spirit then the one sealed is sealed, and God is the one sealing. And everyone is sealed by the father with the holy spirit who from believing God sealed that God is true; and he is sealed so that, having kept the seal and shown it unbroken in the day of redemption, he may be counted together with those being redeemed. [4:31] Let all bitterness and wrath and anger and clamor and blasphemy be taken from you with all malice. Origen says: some thought anger to be a generic passion, and themselves ranked it under the genus desire; and they gave such a definition of anger: anger is desire of punishment of the one who seems to have done wrong not fittingly. pass_b_english: “the sun will go down on your prophets at noon,” so too it goes down on all who sin, and no longer grants them its own rising while they go on sinning. So Paul commands us not to do such things in anger that the sun goes down on us and night comes into our souls.

“And do not give place to the devil” (Ephesians 4:27). Origen says: this is like what is said in Ecclesiastes: “If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, do not leave your place, for healing puts an end to great sins” (Ecclesiastes 10:4). We give place to the devil, or to the ruling spirit when it has risen up against us, whenever our governing faculty has not been filled with holy teachings, or with saving faith and with thoughts that discern and counsel us what is best. For, according to Zechariah the father of John, Satan settles on the regions of the soul; and such assents to what is worse, and leanings toward those assents, invite the devil to come into our souls. So too it is written of Judas the traitor: first, that the devil had already put it into the heart of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, to betray him (John 13:2), and after this, that after the morsel Satan entered into him (John 13:27). So if, when the devil had put it into Judas’s heart to betray the Lord, Judas had stood against what was put there, Satan would not afterward have found a place to enter him.

“Let him who steals steal no longer; rather let him labor, working with his hands what is good, so that he may have something to share with one in need” (Ephesians 4:28). Many of those who are thought to have believed are busy with the affairs of life, and on the pretext of providing for their needs, even if they seem to be clean of idolatry and of all fornication, they do not easily keep from stealing when they buy and sell and do business with others. For this reason he did not hesitate to reproach them, as though some were still stealing (and this in Ephesus), as one who knew people of this kind. The very words “working what is good” point to an honest livelihood. Those who make their living unjustly work not what is good but what is evil; those who reverently secure what they need work what is good in this as well.

“Let no rotten word come out of your mouth, but whatever is good for building up as the need requires, so that it may give grace to those who hear” (Ephesians 4:29). Origen says: the good word, which builds up as the need requires and gives grace to those who hear, is the word that teaches, that urges toward virtue and draws away from vice. The rotten word is the one that feeds vice and stirs people up toward what is worse.

“And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption” (Ephesians 4:30). Grief is a passion, and it is rightly defined as “a fresh opinion that evil is present, at which it is fitting to shrink.” But the Holy Spirit does not form opinions, nor (granting that it does) does it hold the opinion that evil is present to it. If that is so, the Holy Spirit will not be grieved. Is it, then, that as far as it rests with us, we grieve the Holy Spirit of God when we do these things? The Lord too says in Ezekiel, “And in all these things you grieved me” (Ezekiel 16:43). What we have often said about anger and wrath, about sleep and about words that speak of God in human feelings, is useful also for the discussion of “do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God.”

We were sealed with the Holy Spirit so that, receiving the stamp of the Holy Spirit while the one who sealed remains undivided, and taking the impressions of the Holy Spirit, we may become holy; and so that the spirit of the man that is in each of us may become holy, and, I think, the soul as well. The one who is sealed, then, is sealed with the Holy Spirit, but God is the one who seals. Everyone who, by believing God, has set his seal to this, that God is true (John 3:33), is sealed by the Father with the Holy Spirit; and he is sealed so that, by keeping the seal and showing it unbroken on the day of redemption, he may be counted among the redeemed.

“Let all bitterness and wrath and anger and clamor and blasphemy be put away from you, with all malice” (Ephesians 4:31). choices.why: The catena labels are in the printed Greek; they are rendered, and no other third-person remark is added. The old line “Origen links this with Ecclesiastes” was a narrator’s paraphrase of the label.
This is Origen’s own first-person cross-reference in the Greek, not a translator’s note; kept in Origen’s voice.

choices.term: μήποτ' οὖν … λυποῦμεν τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα;
choices.english: Is it, then, that … we grieve the Holy Spirit of God …?
choices.why: A tentative question in the Greek; the old English made it a flat statement.

choices.english: they do not easily keep from stealing … he did not hesitate to reproach them
choices.why: Full causal sentence restored; Origen notes these are people thought to be believers.
Each checked against the KJV verse text. The opening line combines Micah 3:6 and Amos 8:9 and is left uncited.
